subject.title: fix(agents): distinguish terminal aborts from retryable failures (#60388)

question: Should the current PR's boundary be accepted: OpenClaw-owned terminal aborts from run-budget exhaustion, cron terminal timeout strings, HTTP disconnects, restart/shutdown aborts, and marked abortable() wrappers stop fallback, while unmarked provider-owned AbortError/TimeoutError failures remain retryable?
rationale: This is compatibility-sensitive provider routing behavior. Source and live proof support the fix, but automation should not be the final authority on which abort classes are terminal across agent fallback, cron, gateway, and provider-owned failures.

options.title: Accept Current Boundary
options.body: Approve this PR's classification and proceed through exact-head CI and normal merge review.

options.title: Narrow A Terminal Source
options.body: Ask for a targeted change if cron strings, HTTP disconnect tagging, or wrapper cause-chain handling should not stop fallback in all cases.

options.title: Coordinate With Adjacent Fallback Work
options.body: Pause this PR until the related cron budget and stream-abort fallback work is reconciled into one maintainer-owned contract.

recommendation.title: Accept Current Boundary
recommendation.body: Approve this PR's classification and proceed through exact-head CI and normal merge review.

likelyOwner.reason: They supplied live provider proof, authored the latest classification commits, and recently merged the sibling provider-side AbortError fallback behavior.
